mainTopic: A nursing mother's waiting period before remarrying, its exceptions, and the duties of a hired wet nurse
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא about how long a nursing mother must wait before remarrying. רבי מאיר says 24 months and רבי יהודה says 18 months, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל shortens each opinion by three months. אביי relies on lenient rulings to let his tenant farmer get engaged after 15 months. Then רב יוסף tells him that רב and שמואל require a full 24 months. אביי runs after the farmer but cannot catch him, and he learns that one should not rule in front of his teacher. Next a ברייתא lets the mother remarry at once if the baby is with a wet nurse, weaned, or has died. After a debate based on the rule that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his decrees, the גמרא rules that if the baby died she may remarry, but if she weaned him she may not. The amud ends with the duties of a hired wet nurse, the foods that harm milk, and a list of things a mother does that are said to affect her children. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר says 24 months, רבי יהודה says 18 months
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא records a dispute. רבי מאיר says a nursing mother must wait 24 months before remarrying. רבי יהודה allows it after 18 months.
steps.simpleTranslation: She must wait until twenty-four months; this is the opinion of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה permits her after eighteen months.
steps.whatsHappening: We join a ברייתא in the middle. It says how long a nursing mother must wait before she may remarry, and it gives two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiting period protects the baby, who needs to keep nursing. The only question is how long a baby needs that protection. רבי מאיר says 24 months, and רבי יהודה says 18 months.
steps.confusionAlert: The text here begins mid-sentence. The 'she' is a nursing mother whose husband died or divorced her. The waiting period is for the baby's sake, not because of a doubt about who the father is.

phrases.english: Until twenty-four months,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ruling that a nursing mother may not remarry yet, so that the baby can keep nursing.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בִּשְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda permits after eighteen months.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous part of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: 24 months; רבי יהודה: 18 months

steps.title: This is the same argument as בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר יוסף says רבי מאיר is repeating the view of בית שמאי (24 months), and רבי יהודה is repeating the view of בית הלל (18 months).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בר יוסף said: These are exactly the words of בית שמאי, and those are exactly the words of בית הלל. בית שמאי say twenty-four months, and בית הלל say eighteen months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר יוסף shows that this argument is much older. It goes back to בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each opinion has an earlier source behind it. This matters later, because we usually rule like בית הלל. That gives רבי יהודה's 18 months extra weight.
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי later uses this link to בית הלל as one of his reasons for being lenient.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan bar Yosef said:
These are exactly the words of Beit Shammai,
and those are exactly the words of Beit Hillel.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: For Beit Shammai say: twenty-four months,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: שְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: eighteen months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Traces the dispute in step 1 back to an earlier generation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר follows בית שמאי; רבי יהודה follows בית הלל

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל takes three months off each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that under each opinion she may marry three months early, at 21 months or at 15 months. The reason is that a pregnancy does not spoil the milk until three months have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: I will decide. According to the one who says twenty-four months, she may marry at twenty-one months. According to the one who says eighteen months, she may marry at fifteen months. This is because the milk only spoils after three months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a new idea. Under both opinions, she may marry three months before the stated deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that she will become pregnant and her milk will stop. A new pregnancy does not harm the milk for the first three months. So if she marries three months early, the baby still nurses through the full required time.

keyTerms.meaning: I will decide, or settle the matter

steps.confusionAlert: He does not choose between the two opinions. He keeps both and shortens each one by three months.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
I will decide.
According to the one who says twenty-four months,
she is permitted to marry at twenty-one months.
According to the one who says eighteen months,
she is permitted to marry at fifteen months,
because the milk does not become spoiled
phrases.notes: He means spoiled by a new pregnancy.

phrases.english: except after three months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a three-month reduction to both opinions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each opinion's deadline moves three months earlier: 21 months or 15 months

steps.title: עולא and מר עוקבא give lenient rulings
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules like רבי יהודה (18 months). מר עוקבא reports that רבי חנינא let him marry after 15 months.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And מר עוקבא said: רבי חנינא permitted me to marry after fifteen months.
steps.whatsHappening: Later אמוראים now give practical rulings, and both rulings are lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא picks רבי יהודה's 18 months. מר עוקבא goes further and reports that he himself was allowed to marry after 15 months. That matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reading of רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Ulla said: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
And Mar Ukva said:
Rabbi Ḥanina permitted me
phrases.notes: He was allowed to marry a nursing mother.

phrases.english: to marry after fifteen months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives practical rulings on the dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and in practice 15 months was allowed

steps.title: אביי's tenant farmer asks about getting engaged at 15 months
steps.stepSummary: אביי's tenant farmer asks whether he may get engaged to a nursing mother after 15 months.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's tenant farmer came before אביי and asked him: What is the law about getting engaged at fifteen months?
steps.whatsHappening: A real-life story starts here. Someone brings a practical question to אביי, and this sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks only about אירוסין (engagement), not about living together as a married couple. This difference becomes important in אביי's answer.

phrases.english: Abaye's tenant farmer
came before Abaye.
He said to him:
What is the law about getting engaged at fifteen months?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rulings into a real-life case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a man get engaged to a nursing mother after 15 months?

steps.title: אביי allows it and stacks up his reasons
steps.stepSummary: אביי permits the engagement and gives four reasons. We follow רבי יהודה over רבי מאיר. We follow בית הלל over בית שמאי. עולא ruled this way. And מר עוקבא was even allowed to marry at 15 months, so an engagement is surely fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: First, between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. Also, between בית שמאי and בית הלל, the הלכה follows בית הלל. And עולא said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And מר עוקבא said רבי חנינא let him marry after fifteen months, so all the more so you may get engaged.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a yes, and he backs it up with four separate reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two reasons use general rules about whose view we follow. The third and fourth reasons rely on the rulings from step 4. The last reason is a קל וחומר: if full marriage was allowed at 15 months, then engagement alone is surely allowed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
One: between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda,
the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
And furthermore: between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel,
the halakha follows Beit Hillel.
And Ulla said: the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and Mar Ukva said:
Rabbi Ḥanina permitted me
to marry after fifteen months,
so all the more so you, who are only getting engaged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the farmer's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, he may get engaged at 15 months, based on four lenient sources

steps.title: רב יוסף: רב and שמואל require a full 24 months
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells אביי that רב and שמואל both require 24 months. The day of the birth and the day of the engagement are not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי came before רב יוסף, רב יוסף said to him: רב and שמואל both say she must wait twenty-four months, not counting the day the baby was born and not counting the day she gets engaged.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף knocks down אביי's lenient ruling. He cites two great authorities who require the full 24 months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל follow the strict 24 months, and they apply it even to engagement. They do not allow the three-month reduction. Leaving out the first and last days makes the wait even stricter, so all four of אביי's reasons are set aside.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final word on the practical question in this part of the גמרא: a full 24 months.

phrases.english: When he came before Rav Yosef,
phrases.notes: 'He' is אביי, telling his teacher what he had ruled.

phrases.english: he (Rav Yosef) said to him:
Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
she must wait twenty-four months,
not counting the day the baby was born
and not counting the day she becomes engaged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns אביי's lenient answer
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole lenient ruling, even for engagement
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב and שמואל, who are authorities for הלכה in practice, require the full 24 months

steps.title: אביי runs after the farmer but cannot catch him
steps.stepSummary: אביי runs three פרסאות after his tenant farmer to cancel his ruling. Some say it was one פרסה through sand. He does not catch up to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He ran after him three פרסאות, and some say one פרסה through sand, and he did not catch up to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with אביי trying to take back his lenient ruling, but he is too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's run shows that he accepted רב יוסף's correction completely. Even after a ruling has been given, a mistake must be fixed if at all possible.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice we follow רב and שמואל: a full 24 months, even for just getting engaged. The lenient opinions of רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל were not followed in practice here.

phrases.english: He ran after him three parasangs,
phrases.notes: אביי is chasing his tenant farmer to tell him not to rely on the lenient ruling.

phrases.english: and some say one parasang through sand,
and he did not catch up to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows אביי accepting רב יוסף's correction
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי's lenient ruling was mistaken; the הלכה requires 24 months

steps.title: אביי's lesson: don't rule in front of your teacher
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains why one should not give even a simple ruling in his teacher's presence. The reason is not disrespect. It is that he will not succeed in saying it correctly, just as happened to אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Rabbis said a person should not permit even an egg in a milk dish in front of his teacher. That is not because it looks disrespectful. It is because he won't manage to say it right. I knew the ruling of רב and שמואל, and even so I didn't manage to say it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי looks back at his mistake from the last steps and draws a general lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis' rule against ruling before one's teacher applies even to something as obvious as an egg in a milk dish. אביי says the reason is that heaven does not help such a ruling come out right, not that it looks disrespectful. His proof is himself: he knew the 24-month ruling and still ruled wrongly in front of רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg in כותח, a dairy dip. It is an obviously permitted food.
In his teacher's place or presence
The matter will not succeed. He won't get it right.

steps.whatToRemember: Ruling in front of your teacher is avoided even on easy questions, because you won't get it right. אביי's own mistake is the proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the הלכה against giving rulings in the presence of one's רבי.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This thing that the Rabbis said:
even an egg in a dairy dish
phrases.notes: An egg isn't meat, so eating it with milk is clearly fine. That's the point: even something this easy.

phrases.english: a person should not permit in the presence of his teacher,
not because it looks like disrespect,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מִסְתַּיְּיעָא מִילְּתָא לְמֵימְרָא.
phrases.english: but because he will not succeed in saying the matter correctly.
For I had learned it,
this ruling of Rav and Shmuel,
phrases.notes: This is the 24-month rule that רב יוסף told him about in step 7.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא מִסְתַּיְּיעָא לִי מִילְּתָא לְמֵימַר.
phrases.english: and even so I did not succeed in saying it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מִילְּתָא דַאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from אביי's failed ruling and his chase after the farmer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not rule even on an obvious matter before his teacher, because he will not succeed in ruling correctly.

steps.title: A teaching: if the baby no longer nurses, she may remarry at once
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the mother gave her baby to a wet nurse, weaned him, or the baby died, she may remarry immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If she gave her son to a wet nurse, or weaned him, or he died, she is allowed to marry right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives exceptions to the 24-month waiting period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiting period protects the nursing baby. So when the mother is no longer nursing, the ברייתא says the wait no longer applies. The next steps test whether we really follow this ברייתא in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: She is permitted to marry immediately

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If she gave her son to a wet nurse,
or weaned him, or he died,
she is permitted to marry immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: cases where the nursing wait might not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the baby is with a wet nurse, weaned, or has died, the mother may remarry immediately.

steps.title: An old woman reports that רב נחמן forbade it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע plan to rule like the ברייתא. An old woman tells them רב נחמן forbade it in her own case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע thought to rule in practice like this ברייתא. A certain old woman said to them: It happened to me, and רב נחמן forbade me.
steps.whatsHappening: Two חכמים are about to follow the ברייתא in practice. An old woman's story about רב נחמן pushes back against that plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the mother may remarry. The old woman reports that in a real case רב נחמן did not allow it. So the halacha in practice may be stricter than the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: To act in practice, to issue a real ruling
A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua

phrases.aramaic: סְבוּר לְמִיעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא כִּי הָא מַתְנִיתָא.
phrases.english: thought to act in practice in line with this teaching.
A certain old woman said to them:
There was such a case with me,
and Rav Nachman forbade it to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against applying the ברייתא in practice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Challenges acting on the ברייתא's leniency in practice.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן actually ruled strictly in such a case.

steps.title: But רב נחמן allowed it for the ראש גלותא's household
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the old woman's report, because רב נחמן permitted this very thing for the household of the ראש גלותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so?! But רב נחמן permitted it for the household of the ראש גלותא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the old woman's report by pointing out that רב נחמן seems to have ruled the other way elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב נחמן allowed the ראש גלותא's household to remarry after giving the baby to a wet nurse, it seems odd that he forbade it for her. The two reports appear to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This opens a challenge.
The household of the ראש גלותא, the Exilarch who led the Jews of Babylonia

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But Rav Nachman permitted it for them,
for the household of the Exilarch!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַב נַחְמָן שְׁרָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the old woman's report about רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב נחמן forbade remarriage when the baby was given to a wet nurse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן permitted it for the ראש גלותא's household, which seems to contradict the report.

steps.title: The ראש גלותא's household is different
steps.stepSummary: The ראש גלותא's household is a special case, because wet nurses working for them never back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ראש גלותא's household is different, because they don't back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two rulings of רב נחמן are about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a hired wet nurse might quit, and then the remarried mother would have to nurse again. Nobody dares quit on the powerful ראש גלותא, so that worry does not exist there. For ordinary people the worry stays, so רב נחמן forbade it.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not back out of it

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן allows remarriage after hiring a wet nurse only where the nurse surely won't quit, like the ראש גלותא's household. Otherwise it is forbidden.

phrases.english: The Exilarch's household is different,
since they don't back out of it.
phrases.notes: He means the wet nurses they hire would never dare quit, so the baby will surely keep being fed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's two rulings seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ראש גלותא's household is an exception because their wet nurses never back out. Ordinary cases stay forbidden.

steps.title: רב פפי brings a teaching: even unlikely-pregnant women must wait
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי asks רב פפא and רב הונא why they don't learn the prohibition from a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, רבי מאיר requires a three-month wait even for women who almost surely are not pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said to them: Don't you learn it from what was taught? If a woman kept running to her father's house, or was angry while in her husband's house, or her husband was in prison, or went overseas, or was old or sick, or she was barren, old, an אילונית, or a minor, or she miscarried after her husband's death, or cannot give birth, they all must wait three months. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי starts bringing a ברייתא as a source to support forbidding remarriage. The ברייתא shows the Rabbis keep their rules even when the reason seems not to apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-month wait between marriages exists so we can tell who the father of a baby is. רבי מאיר requires it even for women who could hardly be pregnant, so the Rabbis did not make exceptions to their decree. By the same logic, the nursing wait should apply even when the baby is with a wet nurse.

keyTerms.meaning: And don't you hold it? A way of pointing to a source they should already accept.
Always rushing, here to go to her father's house
A woman who never developed physically and cannot have children
To wait three months before remarrying

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two waiting periods. The three months is the wait so we know who the father is. The 24 months is the wait to protect a nursing baby. רב פפי uses the first to shed light on the second.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said to them:
And don't you hold it,
phrases.notes: "It" means the prohibition. He is asking why they don't learn it from the next teaching.

phrases.english: from what was taught:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיְתָה רְדוּפָה לֵילֵךְ לְבֵית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: If she was always rushing to go to her father's house,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ כַּעַס בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ,
phrases.english: or she was angry while in her husband's house,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעְלָהּ חָבוּשׁ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: or her husband was locked up in prison,
or her husband went overseas,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעְלָהּ זָקֵן, אוֹ חוֹלֶה,
phrases.english: or her husband was old, or sick,
or she was barren, or old,
a woman who cannot have children, or a minor,
or one who miscarried after her husband's death,
or one who is unable to give birth,
all of them must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב פַּפֵּי: וְאַתּוּן לָא תִּסְבְּרוּהָ מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back the strict view against following step 10's ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a nursing mother may not remarry even after giving the baby to a wet nurse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר requires a three-month wait even for women who almost surely are not pregnant. The Rabbis' decrees apply even when their reason seems absent.

steps.title: Rule follows רבי מאיר's protective decrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי allows these women to remarry right away, but שמואל rules like רבי מאיר in all his protective decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי permits them to get engaged and marry right away. But רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his decrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי finishes his proof. He shows that the הלכה follows the strict view of רבי מאיר, not the lenient view of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes women wait even when there is almost no chance of a problem. Since שמואל says we follow רבי מאיר's decrees, we should also be strict with a nursing mother. That means she may not remarry early even if she gave the baby to a wet nurse.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with רבי מאיר and is lenient
To get engaged and to marry
His decrees (protective rules that prevent a problem)

steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule about רבי מאיר's decrees is what makes the ברייתא from step 10 hard to rely on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei permits
to be engaged and to marry immediately.
And Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בִּגְזֵירוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof רב פפי began in step 14
steps.raayaObject: A nursing mother may not remarry early, even if the baby is with a wet nurse
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with רבי מאיר vs. רבי יוסי, plus שמואל's rule that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר's decrees

steps.title: The rabbis admit they forgot
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא admit they did not remember this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It was not on our minds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא and רב הונא answer רב פפי. They admit they had forgotten שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They do not argue back. They accept רב פפי's proof, so their plan to rule leniently is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not on our minds; we forgot

phrases.english: They said to him:
It was not on our minds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from steps 14-15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They admit they forgot the rule and accept the proof

steps.title: Final ruling: died is allowed, weaned is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה: if the baby died, the mother may remarry; if she weaned him, she may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: if the baby died, she is permitted. If she weaned him, she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final ruling. It splits the cases from the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby died, there is no baby left to protect, so she may remarry. If she weaned him early, she is forbidden, so women won't stop nursing early just to remarry.
steps.whatToRemember: Baby died → she may remarry. Baby weaned → she may not remarry before the time is up.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
if [the baby] died, she is permitted;
if she weaned him, she is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after the proof is accepted
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A nursing mother whose baby died may remarry right away; one who weaned the baby may not.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי forbids even if the baby died
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says she is forbidden even if the baby died, in case she might kill him in order to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: Even if the baby died, she is also forbidden. Maybe she will kill him and then go and get married.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי disagrees with the lenient half of the ruling. He wants to forbid her even when the baby died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His worry: if a baby's death lets her remarry, a woman might kill her baby to be free. So he would make no exception at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, son of רב אשי

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Even if he died, she is also forbidden,
lest she kill him
and go and get married.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מֵת נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the 'died is permitted' half of step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if the baby died, the mother may not remarry early

steps.title: A real case where a woman strangled her baby
steps.stepSummary: There actually was a case where a woman strangled her child.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident, and she strangled him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real story that seems to support מר בר רב אשי's worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows his fear is not just in theory. It really happened once.

phrases.english: There was an incident, and she strangled him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports מר בר רב אשי's worry with a real event
steps.raayaObject: The worry that a mother might kill her baby to remarry
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real incident where a woman strangled her child

steps.title: That woman was insane
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: that woman was insane, and normal women do not strangle their children.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. That woman was insane, because women do not strangle their children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the story and מר בר רב אשי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One insane woman does not show what normal women do. We do not make a rule for a case that almost never happens, so the ruling of step 17 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling stays: if the baby died, the mother may remarry.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
that woman was insane,
for women do not do this,
strangle their children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the story from step 19 and with it מר בר רב אשי's view
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both the story as proof and מר בר רב אשי's stricter ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was about an insane woman, which says nothing about normal women

steps.title: A hired wet nurse's duties
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a hired wet nurse may not nurse another baby with him, must eat a lot, and may not eat foods bad for milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If they gave her a child to nurse, she may not nurse another baby with him, not her own and not her friend's. Even if she set a small food allowance, she eats a lot. She may not eat things that are bad for milk while nursing him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. A ברייתא lists the rules for a woman hired to nurse someone's baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every rule protects the hired baby's milk. She may not share her milk with another baby, and she must eat well. She must also stay away from foods that hurt her milk.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If they gave her a child to nurse,
she may not nurse along with him
neither her own child nor her friend's child.
If she set a small [allowance],
she eats a lot.
She may not eat, while nursing him,
things that are bad for milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵי שֶׁנָּתְנוּ לָהּ בֵּן לְהָנִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about hired wet nurses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hired wet nurse must protect the hired baby's milk: no other babies, eat a lot, avoid foods bad for milk

steps.title: Why mention a friend's child?
steps.stepSummary: If she may not even nurse her own child, obviously she may not nurse a friend's child. So why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said she may not nurse her own child, do you even need to say a friend's child?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the ברייתא. The second case seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her own child is the case where we would most expect her to be allowed. If even that is forbidden, then a stranger's child should be forbidden even more. So the words 'nor her friend's child' look extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it needed? (it should be obvious)

phrases.english: Now, you said not even her own child;
is her friend's child even necessary to say?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בְּנָהּ אָמְרַתְּ לָא, בֶּן חֲבֶרְתָּהּ מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'nor her friend's child' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her own child is forbidden, a stranger's child is surely forbidden, so the extra case seems unneeded

steps.title: A friend's child might have seemed allowed
steps.stepSummary: You might think only her own child is forbidden, since she would favor him. With a friend's child she would only use extra milk. So the ברייתא tells us both are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: with her own child, whom she loves, she will feed him more. But a friend's child she would only feed if she had extra milk. So the ברייתא teaches us that this is forbidden too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the ברייתא needed to mention a friend's child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases have different risks. With her own child, she might favor him and short the hired baby. With a stranger's child, we might think she only uses leftover milk, so no harm. The ברייתא forbids both.

keyTerms.meaning: She cares about, she has pity on
She lets him suck / feeds him
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: The friend's child is not a 'bigger' case than her own child. It has a different reason you might have allowed it, which is why the ברייתא needs both.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is her own child, whom she cares about,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: that she will feed more.
But her friend's child,
if she did not have extra milk
she would not feed him,
so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: בְּנָהּ הוּא דְּחָיְיסָא עִילָּוֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each case has its own reason it might have been allowed, so both are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only her own child is forbidden, since she would favor him; a friend's child gets only extra milk
steps.terutzMaskana: Both her own child and a friend's child are forbidden

steps.title: Who pays for the nurse's extra food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that the nurse must eat a lot even on a small allowance, and asks where that food comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: if she set a small food allowance, she must still eat a lot. From where does the food come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the ברייתא from step 21 and asks a practical question. This sets up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the nurse must eat a lot even if her agreed food allowance is small. If the allowance doesn't cover it, someone has to pay for the rest. The גמרא wants to know who.

phrases.english: If she set a small amount, she must still eat a lot.
From where?
phrases.notes: He means: where does the extra food come from, if her allowance doesn't cover it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the ברייתא from step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who pays for the extra food the nurse must eat beyond her small allowance.

steps.title: She pays for it herself
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the nurse must buy the extra food with her own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: from her own money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question: the extra food comes out of the nurse's own pocket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She agreed to nurse the baby, so it is her job to keep up a good milk supply. If her allowance is too small, that is her problem, not the family's.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who answers the question

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
From her own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nurse pays for the extra food from her own funds.

steps.title: Which foods are 'bad'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule against eating bad foods and asks which foods it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: she may not eat bad things with him. What are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא and asks what counts as a 'bad' food. This sets up a list of answers from several אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says 'bad things' without naming them. The גמרא wants specific examples of foods that hurt a nursing woman's milk.

keyTerms.meaning: bad things, here meaning foods bad for her milk

phrases.english: She may not eat bad things with him.
phrases.notes: 'With him' means while she is nursing the baby.

phrases.english: What are they?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תֹּאכַל עִמּוֹ דְּבָרִים הָרָעִים מַאי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which foods count as 'bad' for a nursing woman.

steps.title: רב כהנא's list of bad foods
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא gives examples: hops, young green grain, small fish, and soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: for example, hops, young green grain, small fish, and soil.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers with the first list of foods a nursing woman should not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says 'for example,' so this is a sample list, not the full list. That leaves room for the next אמוראים to add more items.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
For example, hops and young green grain,
and small fish and soil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא כְּגוֹן כְּשׁוּת וַחֲזִיז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Hops, young green grain, small fish, and soil.

steps.title: Three more אמוראים add foods
steps.stepSummary: אביי, רב פפא, and רב אשי each add more foods that are bad for nursing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: even pumpkin and quince. רב פפא said: even palm heart and unripe dates. רב אשי said: even כמכא and small fried fish.
steps.whatsHappening: Three more אמוראים each add foods to רב כהנא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one says 'even,' which means he agrees with the earlier list and adds more to it. They are not arguing; they are making the list longer.

keyTerms.meaning: a kind of sharp dip or relish

phrases.english: Abaye said: Even pumpkin and quince.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ קוֹרָא וְכוּפְרָא.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Even palm heart and unripe dates.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ כַּמְכָּא וְהַרְסָנָא.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Even kamka and small fried fish.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read אביי, רב פפא, and רב אשי as disagreeing with רב כהנא. The word 'even' shows each one is adding foods to the list, not replacing it.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more items to רב כהנא's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pumpkin, quince, palm shoots and unripe dates, כמכא, and small fried fish are also bad.

steps.title: Why these foods are harmful
steps.stepSummary: Some of these foods dry up the milk, and some spoil it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of them stop the milk, and some of them spoil the milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the list by explaining why all these foods are a problem for a nursing woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of harm: some foods make her stop producing milk, and some make the milk she has go bad. Either way, the baby suffers, so she must avoid all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: stop or dry up the milk

steps.whatToRemember: A hired wet nurse must pay for her own extra food if her allowance is too small, and she must avoid foods that dry up or spoil her milk.

phrases.english: Some of them stop the milk,
some of them spoil the milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִינַּיְיהוּ פָּסְקִי חֲלָבָא מִינַּיְיהוּ עָכְרִי חֲלָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the whole list from steps 27-28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the listed foods are forbidden because they either dry up the milk or spoil it.

steps.title: How a mother's actions affect her children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists things a woman does, mostly while pregnant, that are said to affect what her children will be like.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who has relations in a mill will have epileptic children. On the ground: long-necked children. One who steps on donkey's blood: bald children. Mustard: gluttonous children. Garden cress: children with runny eyes. Fish brine: children who blink. Clay: ugly children. Strong drink: dark children. Meat and wine: children who are... (continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the nurse's food to a related list: things a mother does that are said to affect her children's bodies and nature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a nurse's food affects the baby's milk, a mother's actions and food during pregnancy are said to affect the child. Each line follows the same pattern: 'one who does X will have children who are Y.' The last line breaks off and continues in the next part of the daf.

keyTerms.meaning: she will have children who are...

phrases.english: One who has relations in a mill:
she will have epileptic children.
One who has relations on the ground:
she will have long-necked children.
One who steps on a donkey's blood:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: she will have bald children.
One who eats mustard:
she will have gluttonous children.
One who eats garden cress:
she will have children with runny eyes.
One who eats fish brine:
she will have children with blinking eyes.
One who eats clay:
she will have ugly children.
One who drinks strong drink:
she will have dark-skinned children.
One who eats meat and drinks wine:
she will have children who are...
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּמְשַׁמְּשָׁא בֵּי רִיחְיָא הָווּ לַהּ בְּנֵי נִכְפֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from foods that affect a nurse's milk to a broader list of a mother's actions that are said to affect her children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mother's actions and foods, especially during pregnancy, are said to affect her children's health, looks, and nature.
